headline: Texas regulator approves ExxonMobil's Rose CCS Class VI permits in 2-1 vote
summary: The Railroad Commission of Texas approved Class VI injection permits for ExxonMobil's Rose CCS project near Beaumont, Jefferson County, clearing three wells to inject roughly 4 Mtpa (about 53 million tonnes over 13 years) from surrounding Gulf Coast industry, over community opposition and one commissioner's dissent.
co2crc_note: A large onshore US Class VI approval granted over community objection is a regulatory-precedent and social-licence data point for Australian storage permitting.
extractor_note: Reported project buildout figure (~US$5bn) is project capex, not a discrete new award; left null per golden rules. 53 Mt is cumulative-over-13-years; annual rate ~4 Mtpa recorded in capacity_mtpa.

headline: Uniper lodges planning application for Killingholme power-station carbon capture
summary: Uniper submitted a planning application to North Lincolnshire Council for a post-combustion capture plant on its consented 550 MW Killingholme CCGT in the UK Humber, designed to capture at least 95% of CO2 and feed a spur pipeline into regional transport-and-storage networks for offshore storage.
co2crc_note: UK gas-power CCS retrofit pathway; a reference case for post-combustion capture on CCGT plant.

headline: Saipem wins EPF contract for enzymatic Bluenzyme capture at Ren-Gas Tampere, Finland
summary: Ren-Gas awarded Saipem the engineering, procurement and fabrication contract for a Bluenzyme 200 enzymatic post-combustion capture unit at its Tampere power-to-gas e-methane plant, set to be Finland's first industrial-scale post-combustion capture unit; the contract becomes effective on Ren-Gas's final investment decision.
co2crc_note: Enzymatic (Bluenzyme) post-combustion capture reaching a commercial EPF contract is relevant to CO2CRC capture-technology tracking for hard-to-abate sources.
extractor_note: Contract value undisclosed; effectiveness conditional on Ren-Gas FID, hence commitment_status 'announced'.

headline: Japanese six-company consortium wins ClassNK AiP for standard 42,000 m3 low-pressure LCO2 carrier
summary: Mitsubishi Shipbuilding, K Line, MOL, NYK, Nihon Shipyard and MILES obtained ClassNK Approval in Principle for a standardised 42,000 m3 low-pressure liquefied-CO2 carrier at Gastech in Bangkok, the first AiP under the MILES standard-design framework, aimed at transporting CO2 captured in Japan to offshore storage as domestic CCS projects ramp up.
co2crc_note: A standardised low-pressure LCO2 carrier design de-risks CO2 shipping and is directly relevant to Australia-Japan and Australia-Timor-Leste (Bayu-Undan) cross-border CO2 export chains.
extractor_note: AiP ceremony 15 Sep at Gastech 2026 Bangkok; broke widely 16 Sep. Design approval milestone, no financial dimension.

headline: BKV completes Barnett Shale upstream, midstream and CCS asset acquisition in Texas
summary: BKV closed its acquisition of Barnett Shale assets adding ~65 MMcfe/d of production and ~117,000 net acres, including an operated CCS project that stored more than 100,000 tonnes of CO2 in the trailing 12 months with its own gas plant, CO2 pipeline and injection well; deal terms were not disclosed.
co2crc_note: A US operator consolidating producing gas with an operating CCS project illustrates the 'closed-loop' capture-plus-storage business model.
extractor_note: Undisclosed M&A consideration; capacity_mtpa 0.1 from '>100,000 t CO2 trailing 12 months' captured by the acquired CCS asset.

headline: Texas regulator approves Exxon's Rose CCS over community objections, defying legislature
summary: Inside Climate News reports that the Railroad Commission of Texas pushed through ExxonMobil's Rose CO2 sequestration permits despite local opposition and a state-legislature stance, spotlighting the community pushback and regulatory-politics tension around a flagship US CCS approval.
co2crc_note: Community opposition and regulator-vs-legislature friction over a flagship US CCS approval is a social-licence signal relevant to Australian storage projects.
extractor_note: Same underlying event as item #01, treated here on its distinct social-licence / regulatory-politics angle.
